source.title: Greedy Coordinate Diffusion: Effective and Semantically Coherent Adversarial Attacks via Diffusion Guidance
source.authors: Bohdan Turbal; Blossom Metevier; Max Springer; A. Korolova

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether adversarial prompts can elicit harmful compliance from safety-aligned chat models, using attack methods and outcome measures different from the fine-tuning and token-position measurements in the cited original studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful-completion attack success rates for several attack methods, including GCG suffixes and GCD's target-prefix optimization, so these outcomes bear on V4. Its diffusion model is given an instruction to generate attacks and uses a prefilled assistant template, but that is not a test of prefilling compliant tokens into the victim model. The text does not measure per-token KL, safety localization in parameters, or the effects of fine-tuning on safety. Cited results from other work and optimization/convergence values that do not report harmful-completion outcomes are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures how often adversarial prompts (GCG suffixes, GCD target-prefix optimization, rewriting attacks) get safety-aligned chat models to comply, against a direct-request baseline. That bears on V4's suffix part. It does not test prefilling the victim or decoding changes. The diffusion attacker's prefilled template is not a victim-side prefill.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors present GCD as a new attack that gets the highest HarmBench ASR with readable prompts, and that keeps working under perplexity and Llama Guard filters. They make no claim about shallow safety alignment, fine-tuning or token depth.
record.recipe_differences: This is an adversarial-prompt attack study, not fine-tuning or per-token KL measurement. It optimizes prompts toward a target affirmative response prefix and evaluates harmful-completion rates.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies by victim model and attack method. The paper also reports lower GCD performance on Llama-3-70B under guard filtering than on the other tested models.
record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2026, Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306
record.problems: The evaluation uses a fixed set of open-weight models and a 48-request subset for the main comparison; the authors report a 1-hour compute cap, 4-bit NF4 quantization, and no transferability evaluation. Defense evaluation covers only perplexity and guard-model filters. The reported main-table ASRs have no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the full set of StrongReject scores for comparator attacks and comparator-method results under perplexity and guard defenses; the selected GCD metrics and main HarmBench ASR comparisons are retained. Also omitted exact target-prefix match rates and target cross-entropy ablations because they are optimization proxies rather than harmful-completion outcomes. Related results appear in Tables 1-3 and Appendix B.1-B.5.

untested.parts: Prefilling a compliant start in the victim and decoding changes were not tested. Only GCG is a suffix attack. The other attacks rewrite or optimize prompts.
No analysis of parameters or ranks.
No test of data or objective causes.

missing.what: GCG on unquantized (FP16) Llama-3-8B: 25.00% HarmBench ASR and 0.1694 StrongReject score, against 0.00% when 4-bit quantized
Perplexity-filter ASR for the comparator attacks, notably GCG and GBDA falling to 0.00% on Qwen, Mistral and Llama-3-70B. This bears on whether suffix attacks survive a simple defence.

record.verdict_notes: The study is about attack methods, so only V4 is loosely relevant, and mostly for the 'defeats refusal' reading rather than prefill/suffix/decoding. The main V4-relevant evidence is the GCG rows and the GCD target-prefix optimization. Several record rows (controls, own-method ablations, defense-filter rows) should not carry V4 links. All attacks use 4-bit quantized models and a 48-request subset, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and resulting refusal rates.
Fine-tuning on benign data and resulting harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
The study evaluates adversarial prompt attacks, including GCG suffix attacks, but does not isolate victim-model prefilled compliant openings or decoding changes as interventions.
Whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Training to deepen safety and whether such training holds up.

relationships.condition: GCD target-prefix optimization (prompts optimized so the model starts with 'Sure, here is...') on Llama-3-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B, Mistral-7B and Llama-3-70B (4-bit, 48 requests)
relationships.reason: GCD pushes HarmBench ASR from 4.17% direct baseline to 85.42%, 97.92% and 70.83% on the three Llama/Qwen victims, and to 100% on Mistral from 52.08% (r08, r16, r24, r32). The attack optimizes for a compliant opening, which fits V4's 'getting past the opening'.
relationships.display_finding: GCD raised HarmBench ASR from a 4.17% direct baseline to 85.42%, 97.92% and 70.83% on the three Llama and Qwen victims, and from 52.08% to 100% on Mistral.

source_check.reason: r08, r16, r24 and r32 correctly report GCD ASR, but GCD constructs whole prompts. An affirmative-prefix optimization objective does not itself test victim prefilling, appended suffixes or victim-decoding changes, or isolate getting past the opening as the cause of compliance.

relationships.condition: GCG suffix on 4-bit quantized Llama-3-8B and Llama-3-70B
relationships.reason: GCG gets 0.00% on Llama-3-8B and 4.17% on Llama-3-70B, no gain over direct request (r02, r26). The authors attribute this to quantization and a 1-hour compute cap. The FP16 Llama-3-8B result of 25.00% is in a footnote with no row. This limits the suffix part of V4 to a setup-dependent result rather than a clean challenge.
relationships.display_finding: GCG gets 0.00% on Llama-3-8B and 4.17% on Llama-3-70B, no gain over direct requests. The authors attribute this to quantization and a 1-hour compute cap, and report 25.00% on FP16 Llama-3-8B.

source_check.condition: GCG suffix on 4-bit quantized Llama-3-8B and Llama-3-70B
source_check.reason: The effect is absent in this condition group: GCG gives 0.00% versus 4.17% direct-request ASR on Llama-3-8B, and 4.17% versus 4.17% on Llama-3-70B (r02, r26). Quantization and compute qualifications restrict the challenge's scope; they do not change an absent effect into an incomplete effect.
